title: Applied ML Evals Integration: Onboarding, Benchmarks, Guardrails, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook describes Redwood's integrated applied-ML evals workflow: how we onboard models into the eval harness, maintain prompt sets and benchmarks, apply quality guardrails and quantization profiles, and run a structured regression triage process. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and platform owners responsible for model onboarding, continuous evaluation, and production quality monitoring.

Goals

- Provide a single reference for the end-to-end eval lifecycle: onboarding -> baseline benchmarking -> production guardrails -> regression triage.
- Ensure repeatable, automatable checks with clear owners and SLOs.
- Reduce production regressions and speed up remediation through prioritized triage.

Scope

This document covers: eval harness configuration, prompt set curation, benchmark definitions and metrics, quantization profile selection, automated guardrails (quality tests), and a step-by-step regression triage playbook. It does not cover model training experiments or hyperparameter tuning.

Owners and Roles

- Document owner: Applied-ML team (owner: Ava Chen)
- Eval harness platform: Eng - Serving Runtime (primary owner: Rafael Gomez)
- Model onboarding review: Research / Applied ML (primary reviewer: Maya Singh)
- Regression triage coordinator: Eng SRE (primary: Noah Park)
- Escalation path: Product & Customer Success for customer-impacting regressions

Definitions

- Eval harness: Redwood's automated test runner for model quality and performance checks.
- Prompt set: A curated set of inputs and expected behaviors (gold labels or pass/fail criteria).
- Quality guardrail: An automated check (metric threshold or classifier) that flags unacceptable outputs.
- Quantization profile: Model conversion settings (precision, operators, calibration data) used for cost/perf trade-offs.

Onboarding checklist (required before a model is certified for internal experiments)

1) Model metadata submitted to model-catalog: architecture, weights, license, expected input/output shapes, tokenizer version, and known compatibility notes.
2) Local smoke tests: start/run inference on representative inputs; verify deterministic initialization and basic tokenization.
3) Eval harness baseline run: run the standard eval suite (see "Eval harness config") and record baseline metrics.
4) Prompt sets selection: map the model to existing prompt sets (or create new) for the customer domains it will target.
5) Quantization compatibility check: run the quantization profile compatibility tests (see quantization table).
6) Security/compliance checklist: data handling review for PII-sensitive prompts and KMS checks for Private deployments.
7) Sign-off: Research lead + Serving Runtime owner + Applied-ML owner.

Eval harness configuration (example)

The eval harness is launched by CI with the following config fragment (YAML):

pipeline: eval-run
platform: eval-harness
model: "<model-id>"
prompts: "prompt-sets/<domain>.jsonl"
benchmarks: ["accuracy", "toxicity", "factuality", "latency"]
quantization_profiles: ["int8-calibrated", "fp16-fused"]
output: s3://redwood-evals/<model-id>/runs/<run-id>/
reporting: slack:#applied-ml-evals,s3

Core benchmark definitions and expected metrics

- Accuracy (domain-specific): F1 / exact match as applicable on gold-labeled prompt sets. Target: >= 0.88 for core product domains; lower-bound warning at 0.80.
- Toxicity: Jigsaw-style classifier failure rate. Threshold: < 0.5% for high-sensitivity domains; warning at 1.0%.
- Factuality: Supported by targeted QA prompts with human adjudication sampling. Target: no statistically significant drop vs baseline (p < 0.05).
- Latency: 95th percentile token-generation latency under targeted load profile. SLO: p95 < 200ms for hosted tiers; p95 < 120ms for Dedicated with pinned capacity.

Example prompt set structure (JSONL per-line)

{"id": "p0001", "input": "Summarize the following email in one sentence:\n...", "expected_behavior": "concise summary; person names redacted"}
{"id": "p0002", "input": "Is the following statement true or false:\n...", "gold_label": "false"}

Prompt curation guidelines

- Each prompt set should have 500–5,000 examples for core product domains; 100–500 for low-volume domains.
- Labeling: At least two human labels per example, conflict resolution policy applied.
- Coverage: Include edge-cases, adversarial inputs, and common user paraphrases.
- Metadata: include domain, difficulty, and source (synthetic/human).

Quality guardrails (automated)

- Pre-commit checks (syntactic): tokenizer mismatch, shape errors.
- Nightly checks (functional): accuracy on core prompt sets, toxicity, and hallucination proxies.
- Canary checks (production-like): sampling from live traffic with masked PII — run automated classifiers and human-in-the-loop review for samples that fail thresholds.
- Alerts: PagerDuty when production-impacting metrics exceed thresholds (see Monitoring & SLOs).

Quantization profiles and compatibility (summary table)

Profile | Description | Use-case | Test gate
int8-calibrated | Per-channel int8 with calibration dataset | Max cost reduction; best for batch workloads | Pass accuracy delta <= 1.5% vs baseline
fp16-fused | Mixed FP16 ops with fused kernels | Latency-sensitive inference with moderate cost savings | Pass latency improvement >= 10% without accuracy loss > 0.5%
int8-ptq | Post-training quantization (no calibration) | Fastest conversion; fall-back when calibration not available | Pass only for non-critical domains; human review required

Regression triage playbook (step-by-step)

1) Detection: A regression is detected by automated monitoring (nightly evals) or a reported customer issue.
2) Triage intake: Regression coordinator (Eng SRE) creates a triage ticket with: model-id, run-id, metric delta, affected prompt sets, and sample outputs.
3) Reproduce: Run the eval-harness with the exact model commit/docker image under identical config. Reproduce failure and record logs, seed, and RNG state.
4) Breadth assessment: Identify scope — is the regression domain-specific, prompt-set-wide, or general? Run quick A/B: baseline vs candidate across key prompt sets.
5) Root-cause hypotheses: shortlist probable causes in order: 1) model weights change, 2) tokenizer changes, 3) quantization profile mismatch, 4) eval harness/metric bug, 5) data/regression in prompt set.
6) Causal tests: For each hypothesis run targeted checks (e.g., run candidate model with baseline quantization; run baseline model with candidate quantization; compare tokenization outputs).
7) Fix and verify: Apply fix (rollback, adjust quantization, patch harness) in a staging environment. Re-run full eval harness run and canary on live-sampled traffic if applicable.
8) Communicate: Update triage ticket with root cause, fix, and mitigation plan. Notify stakeholders: Product, Customer Success, and affected customers if external impact.
9) Postmortem: For P1 regressions or repeated failures, create a short postmortem with timeline, RCA, mitigation, and action items assigned.

Priority and escalation matrix

- P0: Customer-facing production regressions causing incorrect or unsafe outputs impacting >1% of traffic or violating compliance. PagerDuty and immediate rollback.
- P1: Significant metric drop in nightly evals with risk to customers. Triage within 4 hours; notify Product.
- P2: Minor metric drift or infra-related failures. Triage within 48 hours.

Monitoring & SLOs (examples)

- Nightly eval coverage: 100% of certified models run nightly.
- Regression detection latency: 95% of regressions detected within 24 hours of introduction.
- Eval harness flakiness: CI false-positive rate < 2%.
- Alert thresholds: accuracy delta > 5% (P0 warn), toxicity delta > 0.5% (P1 warn), latency p95 increase > 30ms (P1).

Automation and CI integration

- CI jobs: on PR to model-catalog and on model-build artifact publish.
- Gate PRs with quick smoke eval (subset of prompts) and require full eval pass for merge to main.
- Artifact tagging: model artifacts must include eval-run-id, quantization-profile, and baseline-metrics in metadata.

Example CLI commands

# Run the eval harness locally for quick reproduction
redwood-eval run --model <model-id> --prompts prompt-sets/support.jsonl --benchmarks accuracy,toxicity --output ./runs/<run-id>

# Compare baseline vs candidate (A/B script)
redwood-eval compare --baseline s3://redwood-evals/<model-a>/latest --candidate ./runs/<model-b> --metrics accuracy,toxicity,latency --report ./compare-report.json

Human review workflow (for high-sensitivity failures)

1) Auto-flagging: harness flags samples above toxicity/factuality thresholds.
2) Human queue: samples appear in the Human Review dashboard with annotations.
3) Two independent reviewers: assign two reviewers for adjudication; tie-break by senior reviewer.
4) Update prompt set: if failure indicates prompt-label issue, update prompt set and re-run baseline.
